is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluated Anopheles darlingi, Anopheles triannulatus s.l., Anopheles dunhami, and Anopheles squamifemur (Page 8, Table 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper focuses on 16S rRNA profiling of mosquito microbiota and does not genotype any target insecticide resistance markers (target markers mentioned on Page 16 were only cited as background literature).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No resistance marker genotype or allele frequency data are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in San Pedro de los Lagos, Leticia, Amazonas, Colombia (South America) (Page 4, Section 2.2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study investigating mosquito microbiota through field collection and 16S rRNA gene sequencing.

sub_country_location.evidence: San Pedro de los Lagos, Leticia, Amazonas, Colombia (4°08'32.3" S 69°57'13.8" W) (Page 4, Section 2.2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Samples were collected in November 2023 and January 2024 (Page 5, Section 2.2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Field samples collected specifically for this primary microbiome study in Colombia.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary files needed since the study does not contain target marker genotyping data.

assessment.summary: This study characterized the bacterial microbiota associated with different life stages and breeding sites of Anopheles species in Leticia, Amazonas, Colombia, using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. The study did not perform insecticide resistance marker genotyping or bioassays.
exclusion_reasons: The study does not report genotyping for any target insecticide-resistance markers.
The study does not report extractable genotype data.
The mosquito populations were collected in Colombia (South America), not in Africa.
